name: conversus
description: Run competitive multi-agent deliberations — structured adversarial reviews, red-team proposals, and consensus building with game theory modes
long_description:
Make better decisions by pitting AI agents against each other in structured debate. Ask a question like "Should we use Postgres or MongoDB?" and conversus runs a 5-phase pipeline (review → cross-review → revision → disputes → synthesis) where multiple agents with different perspectives argue, critique each other, and converge on a grounded verdict. Unlike single-LLM answers that sound confident even when they're wrong, conversus surfaces the adversarial record so you can see HOW the answer was produced.

Three tools ship in this bundle:

• conversus_decide — ask an ad-hoc question, get a deliberated answer. No config needed.
• conversus_run — run a full deliberation from a YAML config with your own agents and target documents.
• conversus_validate — estimate the LLM launch cost of a config before committing to a real run.

Supports 8 game theory modes: cooperative, winner-take-all, prisoner's dilemma, red-blue, negotiation, resource-allocation, fair-division, and mechanism-design. Works with anthropic, openai, claude-code, ollama, gemini, and 5 more providers. This bundle is self-contained — no separate Python or pip install required.

tools.name: conversus_decide
tools.description: Run an ad-hoc deliberation on a natural-language question using the built-in pragmatist + devil's advocate agents. Best for quick decisions — no config file needed. Accepts a mode parameter (cooperative, red-blue, winner-take-all, prisoners-dilemma).

tools.name: conversus_run
tools.description: Run or parse a full multi-agent deliberation from a YAML config file. Supports all 8 game theory modes, custom agents, target documents, and optional arbiters. Use this when you want reproducible deliberations with your own stakeholder personas.

tools.name: conversus_validate
tools.description: Validate a conversus YAML config and estimate the total LLM launch count BEFORE running. Catches schema errors, missing target files, and invalid mode names. Always run this before a real deliberation to know the cost.
